paras: The mob hanging of John Russell took place near Saltillo, Indiana, on Friday, about 2 September 1881, when a man arrested on a charge of stealing a watch was taken from an officer and hanged up three times to make him confess. Russell survived after being revived with difficulty, and he protested his innocence throughout. The episode is known only from a one-paragraph wire brief reprinted in several daily papers; no local Indiana report was found.

Russell had been arrested on a charge of stealing a watch and was in an officer's hands when he was seized. In most copies of the brief he was taken from the officer "by a mob", though the Daily Gazette's version says only that he was taken from an officer. His captors "hanged up" Russell three times "to extort a confession." The last time he was strung up, blood gushed from his nose and mouth, and he was resuscitated only with difficulty.
None of the reports gives Russell's race, the number of men in the mob, the time of day, or where near Saltillo the hanging took place.
No report of arrests, charges against the mob, or the outcome of the theft charge against Russell appears in the coverage.

The brief ran on 5 September 1881 on the front pages of the Daily Gazette, the Lancaster Daily Intelligencer and the Daily Republican, and on 7 September in the Savannah Morning News. Each paper set it without a headline among unrelated items in a general news column, such as the Intelligencer's "Latest News by Mail" and the Republican's "Everywhere." The copies differ only in small details: the victim appears as "John T. Russell," "John C. Russell" and "John C. Russel," and the Republican omits the watch. No paper added comment, though every version closed with the line that he "protested his innocence all the time."

reader.title: Mob hanging of John Russell near Saltillo, Indiana
bases: A man under arrest was taken from an officer, by a mob in three of four versions, and hanged up three times to force a confession, but survived and no attempt to kill him is reported (A1, A2, A3).

Russell was resuscitated and no death is reported, so the standard definition is not met; the seizure from an officer and hanging to extort a confession over a theft charge were extralegal and done under a pretext of justice, by 'a mob' of unstated size (A1, A2, A3).
All four reports are word-for-word copies of one wire brief, with no local or follow-up account (A1, A2, A3, A4).
